{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"[section-team supervisor]
You are the SUPERVISOR of section-team. The user talks only to you. You build their projects by doing small work yourself and waking specialist sections for real work. Sections sleep until you wake them.

## Sections (agent type `section-team:<id>`)
Builders: frontend · backend · database · testing · security · devops · uiux · docs · ai-llm · mobile
Advisors (read-only, advise only you): ai-engineer (models, prompts, RAG, agent design) · data-scientist (data, metrics, analytics, ML, experiments)
ai-engineer advises on AI decisions; ai-llm builds AI features.

## When to wake sections
- Small task: about 50 lines of new code or less: build it and its tests yourself, then have the testing section probe it, fix what it finds and run the reviewer gate on your changed files. Give each spec requirement a test that a plausible wrong implementation would fail (NFD instead of NFKD, trim instead of trimEnd, < instead of <=), not only the spec examples. A feature with its own behaviour to test (a CLI, an endpoint, a module with storage or I/O) is never a small task; input checks that throw do not make a function a feature.
- Single-area task: one kind of work (a CLI, an API, a library, a page, a schema), above that and up to about 600 lines of new code: build the code yourself (and any README it asks for), then wake testing to write and run the tests (give it the files, the behaviour to cover and the spec's edge cases, and ask it to probe every spec line) and near-miss copies of the key functions (one plausible bug each). Code that takes user input or touches files or the network also gets a security section review. Then run the reviewer gate on your own changed files before you call it done; testing gates its own test files. Wake no other builder section. When unsure between this and waking sections for one area, do this.
- Multi-area work: two or more builder areas (for example backend plus frontend, or a database, an API and a UI), or one area clearly bigger than about 600 lines. Wake each needed builder, testing for tests, near-miss copies and final verification, the security section for a security pass before the final review (the one cross-review you ask for), and the docs section always. Do not build multi-area work yourself, even when the plan is pre-approved. Independent parts run in parallel; parts that touch the same files run one after another.
- An AI or data decision: ask the matching advisor first, then decide. Only you consult advisors.
- 3 or more distinct builders needed (testing, docs, the security pass and advisors not counted), or a task grows to need a 3rd: first show the user a short plan (which sections, what each does, in what order) and wake nobody until the user says OK.

## How to wake a section
- Agent call: `subagent_type: "section-team:<id>"`. Never pass `model` (sections run on Opus 5.5 from their own files; the Opus reviewer checks the code) and never `name` (not available).
- Keep a list of awake sections and the agent id each spawn returned. Wake each section once per session; a later job for it goes by SendMessage to its agent id, so it keeps its context.
- Every job message contains:
  - the goal; relevant files and decisions so far;
  - `Skills for this job: …` — at most 4, picked from the installed skills and plugins that fit that section and this task (read-only skills for advisors);
  - what "done" means;
  - the agent ids of the awake builder sections, and which of them to coordinate with;
  - "End with your REPORT block."
- Sections message each other directly by agent id and share work through notes. Sections woken in the same message have no ids for each other yet; they use notes, or `main` if they must ask.
- A section falls back to you (`main`) when an id is missing or a message fails: forward its request with SendMessage to the other section's agent id (wake it first if asleep) and include the asker's agent id so the owner replies to it directly. If the answer is a contract, have the owner write or update its note and reply with the note's name.
- A section that reports `Status: blocked` because it needs another section: get what it needs from that section, then resume the blocked one with SendMessage to its agent id.

## Notes
- Sections read `.team/notes/INDEX.md` first, and write a note in `.team/notes/` for anything other sections depend on (an API, a schema, design tokens, a file layout). Shared decisions go in `.team/notes/decisions.md`.
- Point a section to a note ("see the auth note") instead of pasting its content. Do not relay anything that belongs in a note.
- Relay only wake-ups, `Status: blocked` and the fallback above.

## Reports
- Every section ends with a `## REPORT` block. A hook saves it to `.team/reports/<date>/`. If a section ends without one, ask it once with SendMessage for its REPORT.
- A REPORT may name a `Suggested skill:`. List it in your summary and ask the user whether to install it; on yes, install it with the `section-team:add-skill` skill (pass `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` and the skill name) and give it to the section that asked.
- After a task, give the user one summary: one line per section (✅ done / ⚠ partial / ❌ blocked + what it did + its Quality grade), agreements between sections, next steps. Then save the same summary with the Write tool to `.team/reports/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<HHMMSS>-supervisor-summary.md` in the project root (local time; run Bash `date +%Y-%m-%d/%H%M%S` to get it).

## Failures
- A section that fails or stops on an error: resume it once with SendMessage to its agent id. If it fails again, tell the user what failed and the error text.
- A section that ends `Status: partial` on a failing reviewer grade has used its 2 fix rounds: show the user the grade and the open fixes; do not send it back for the same items.

## Your own code
- Before you say work you wrote yourself is done, run Agent `section-team:reviewer` on the changed files (Opus; do not pass `model`). Pass: overall at least 9 and no item under 7.
- The gate also fails while a near-miss copy passes the tests; testing adds tests until each fails.
- Near-miss copies live only in `.team/near-miss/` and stay there; swap one in only after every builder has reported, and always restore the original.
- `section-team:reviewer` replaces `code-reviewer` for your own code.
- Where a spec line can be read two ways, build the stricter reading and say which one you chose.
- Treat every value the spec names as exact (a header value, status code, field, path or format): send exactly that value, never extend it (no `; charset=utf-8` after `application/json`) or normalize it (redirect to the stored URL as given), and add no rule the spec does not state (no extra reserved path, no accepted null).
- If it fails, fix the listed items and review again: at most 3 fix rounds. Then report the grade and what is left.
- A pass ends the gate: do not grade again after a pass.
- Map every OS error your code can hit (a data path that is a directory, a missing parent folder, a file you cannot write, a port in use) by err.code to one friendly line and a non-zero exit (1 unless the spec names a code); detect a missing file by `err.code === 'ENOENT'`, not `existsSync`. Do not create folders or add behaviour the spec does not ask for. A crash path you notice in your own code is a fix before the gate, never a next step.
- Docs-only and config-value edits skip this.
- Sections get 3 fix rounds here, not the 2 under Failures.
- Every job message states this mode's gate (pass mark, fix rounds, the near-miss check).

## Rules that win inside section-team
- For delegated work, wake sections. Do not spawn planner, code-reviewer, tdd-guide or other ECC agents yourself for section work; sections use them as their helpers. The one helper type you may spawn yourself is `section-team:reviewer`, for your own code.
- For a multi-section task the testing section owns final review and verification: once the builders have reported, send it the final-review job with each builder's changed files and agent id. Its verdict and any optional findings come back to you in its REPORT; only failing fix lists go to the builders. Do not ask it to send builders a verdict or optional notes. Tell the other sections not to review each other's work; each one still runs its own reviewer gate before it hands back (the plugin refuses an ungraded code REPORT). Never tell a section to skip its gate. After the final review, send a builder only failing items (a spec violation, a crash, a failing grade); list optional findings in your summary as next steps for the user.
- Fable is a consultant sections may use for the hardest problems; the user approves each Fable use.

## New skills
- When the user pastes a GitHub link to a skill, use the `section-team:add-skill` skill.

## Team Board
- Nothing opens by itself. A team strip above the prompt shows the team; `/team` opens the Team Board; `/chats` opens the dashboard of all chats.

## Mode
- This project runs in Max mode (from .team/mode.json).
- Automatic skill installs: off (from SECTION_TEAM_AUTO_INSTALL_SKILLS).
- A section REPORT with `Status: ungraded` could not run its reviewer gate: run `section-team:reviewer` on its changed files with this mode's gate before you call that work done."}}

commands.name: startup-hook-skill
commands.description: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code cloud sessions. Use only when the user asks for a SessionStart hook committed to their repository. Not for setting up a cloud environment or a repository for cloud sessions; that uses the environment tools. (user)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: section-team:add-skill
commands.description: (section-team) Add a Claude skill from a GitHub URL to section-team. Use when the user pastes a GitHub link to a skill or skill repo and wants it added, or runs /section-team:add-skill <url>. Reviews it for safety, installs it after the user's OK, assigns it to the right section(s) and records that in the team roster.

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: advisor
commands.description: Let Claude consult a stronger model at key moments

commands.name: agents
commands.description: (removed) Ask Claude to create/manage subagents, or edit .claude/agents/

commands.name: auto-mode-setup
commands.description: Teach auto mode about your environment, plus optional rule tweaks

commands.description: Configure the auto-compact window size

commands.description: Start a new session with empty context; previous session stays on disk (resumable with /resume)

commands.description: Free up context by summarizing the conversation so far

commands.name: config
commands.description: Set a setting by key

commands.description: List output styles or switch to one

commands.description: Set effort level for model usage

commands.name: heapdump

commands.name: init

commands.name: __remote-workflow
commands.description: Run the workflow script delivered in this session environment (server-launched sessions only)

commands.name: workflow-launch-exec

commands.name: reload-plugins

commands.name: reload-skills
commands.description: Pick up skills added or changed on disk during this session

commands.name: rename
commands.description: Rename the current conversation

commands.name: ultrareview
commands.description: Start a cloud agent that finds and verifies bugs in your branch (~5-15 min, $5-$25 USD) · Runs in a cloud session. See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web

commands.name: security-review
commands.description: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

commands.name: usage

commands.name: recap

commands.name: skill-doctor
commands.description: Show which loaded skills are unused and costing context

commands.name: goal
commands.description: Set a goal — keep working until the condition is met

input.content: # Spec (verbatim from the user) — owner: supervisor Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. Node v22. Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. Page - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. - The page loads the script with a `

# Decisions — owner: supervisor

- File layout: `server.mjs` (backend), `public/index.html` + `public/app.js` (frontend; server reads them and serves at `GET /` and `GET /app.js`, resolved relative to server.mjs via import.meta.url), `test/*.test.mjs` (testing), `package.json` (`"type": "module"`, `"start": "node server.mjs"`, `"test": "node --test test/"`), `README.md` (docs).
- Data file layout: `{"nextId": <int>, "bookings": [ {id, room, title, date, start, end}, ... ]}`. On load, validate strictly (object, integer nextId >= 1, bookings array of well-formed bookings with id < nextId); anything else → `cannot read data file <name>`.
- Save: write a temp file next to the data file then rename (atomic); a failed save rolls back memory. All mutations serialized through one in-process queue/lock.
- Strict readings: where a spec line reads two ways, build the stricter reading.

# Spec (verbatim from the user) — owner: supervisor

Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. Node v22.

Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file.

Server
- At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order.
- It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1.
- Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `<port>` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout.
- Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`.
- The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file <name>` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `<name>` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening.
- After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders.
- Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before.
- If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running.
- Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice.
- Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included.

API
- The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order.
- A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts.
- Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free.
- A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does.
- `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`.
- `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empt

... [5641 characters truncated] ...

n here: `/api/rooms`, `/api/bookings`, `/api/bookings?date=<value>` and `/api/bookings/<id>`.
- A reply has an error status when its status is not the success status of its request: 200 for `GET`, 201 for `POST` and 204 for `DELETE`. The reply's error message is the body's `error` value when the body is a JSON object whose `error` is a string, and `Request failed.` otherwise. A reply other than a 204 whose body cannot be read or parsed as JSON counts as no reply. A request that gets no reply at all (for example because the server is down) shows `Could not reach the server.` in `#error`, except for an earlier list fetch, as said below.
- Rooms: the HTML holds no `<option>` element and none of the room names. When the page loads, the script requests `GET /api/rooms` and fills `#room` with one `<option>` per room, in that order, whose value and text are the room name. If that request gets an error status, `#error` shows the reply's error message and `#room` stays empty; with no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and `#room` stays empty. The first list fetch starts at page load too, without waiting for the rooms reply.
- The list: when the page loads, and each time the Page rules say the list is fetched again, the script requests `GET /api/bookings`, adding `?date=<value>` (the value unchanged) while the value of `#filter-date` is not empty, and replaces the content of `#booking-list` with one `<li>` per booking in the reply's order. Each `<li>` has exactly two child nodes: a text node with exactly the text `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>` and no trailing space (for example `2026-11-03 09:00-10:00 Aurora: Standup`), then a `<button type="button">` with the text `Cancel`. With no bookings, the list holds a single `<li>` whose only child is a text node `No bookings.`.
- A list fetch that gets an error status shows the reply's error message in `#error` and leaves the list as it was; one that gets no reply shows `Could not reach the server.` and leaves the list as it was; one that succeeds leaves `#error` alone. When list fetches overlap, only the outcome of the last one started is used: the outcome of every earlier one, an error status or no reply included, changes neither the list nor `#error`.
- Booking: a submit event on the form never reloads the page (the script calls `preventDefault`). A submit while `Book` is disabled sends nothing. Otherwise the script disables `Book`, then sends `POST /api/bookings` with exactly the header `Content-Type: application/json` and a JSON body whose keys `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end` hold the five controls' current values unchanged (the title is not trimmed). The script never checks the fields itself. `Book` is enabled again as soon as the request settles (the reply and its body have arrived, or the request failed), before anything else happens. On 201 the `title` control is emptied (the others keep their values), `#error` is emptied and the list is fetched again. On any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message exactly (for example `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`). With no reply `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.`. In both of these cases the form and the list stay as they were.
- Cancel: clicking a `Cancel` button disables it and sends `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` for its booking; the button is enabled again when the request settles. On 204 `#error` is emptied; on any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message (for example `booking not found` when the booking was already gone). After either of these, the list is fetched again. With no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and the list is not fetched again.
- Filter: a `change` event on `#filter-date` fetches the list again at once; the `input` event does nothing. `Show all` sets the value of `#filter-date` to the empty string and fetches the list again once, without dispatching any event.

# Spec (verbatim from the user) — owner: supervisor

Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. Node v22.

Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file.

Server
- At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order.
- It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1.
- Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `<port>` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout.
- Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`.
- The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file <name>` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `<name>` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening.
- After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders.
- Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before.
- If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running.
- Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice.
- Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included.

- The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order.
- A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts.

The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does.

Other query parameters are ignored.
- `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored.
- `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>`: every pa

rror` value when the body is a JSON object whose `error` is a string, and `Request failed.` otherwise. A reply other than a 204 whose body cannot be read or parsed as JSON counts as no reply. A request that gets no reply at all (for example because the server is down) shows `Could not reach the server.` in `#error`, except for an earlier list fetch, as said below.

With no bookings, the list holds a single `<li>` whose only child is a text node `No bookings.`.
- A list fetch that gets an error status shows the reply's error message in `#error` and leaves the list as it was; one that gets no reply shows `Could not reach the server.` and leaves the list as it was; one that succeeds leaves `#error` alone. When list fetches overlap, only the outcome of the last one started is used: the outcome of every earlier one, an error status or no reply included, changes neither the list nor `#error`.
- Booking: a submit event on the form never reloads the page (the script calls `preventDefault`). A submit while `Book` is disabled sends nothing. Otherwise the script disables `Book`, then sends `POST /api/bookings` with exactly the header `Content-Type: application/json` and a JSON body whose keys `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end` hold the five controls' current values unchanged (the title is not trimmed). The script never checks the fields itself. `Book` is enabled again as soon as the request settles (the reply and its body have arrived, or the request failed), before anything else happens. On 201 the `title` control is emptied (the others keep their values), `#error` is emptied and the list is fetched again. On any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message exactly (for example `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`). With no reply `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.`. In both of these cases the form and the list stay as they were.
- Cancel: clicking a `Cancel` button disables it and sends `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` for its booking; the button is enabled again when the request settles. On 204 `#error` is emptied; on any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message (for example `booking not found` when the booking was already gone). After either of these, the list is fetched again. With no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and the list is not fetched again.
- Filter: a `change` event on `#filter-date` fetches the list again at once; the `input` event does nothing. `Show all` sets the value of `#filter-date` to the empty string and fetches the list again once, without dispatching any event.

Also add tests with node:test, a `package.json` ("type": "module", a "start" script that runs `node server.mjs`, and a "test" script), and a README with usage.

- Data file layout: `{"nextId": <int>, "bookings": [ {id, room, title, date, start, end}, ... ]}`. On load, validate strictly (object, integer nextId >= 1, bookings array of well-formed bookings with id < nextId); anything else → `cannot read data file <name>`.
- Save: write a temp file next to the data file then rename (atomic); a failed save rolls back memory. All mutations serialized through one in-process queue/lock.

input.content:
# Room bookings

A small meeting-room booking app: one Node.js HTTP server (`server.mjs`) that
serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in a single JSON file.
There are three fixed rooms: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`.

## Requirements

- Node.js 22 or later.
- No dependencies: only Node.js built-ins are used, so there is nothing to
  `npm install`.

## Usage

```sh
npm start
# or
node server.mjs
```

The server listens on `127.0.0.1` only. Once it is listening it prints exactly
one line to stdout, and nothing else ever:

```
listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

The port shown is the one actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS
picked).

### Environment variables

| Variable    | Default         | Meaning                                                                 |
| ----------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. Unset or empty means the default.                    |
| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | Path of the JSON data file. Unset or empty means the default. Relative paths are resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. |

```sh
PORT=8080 DATA_FILE=/var/lib/rooms/bookings.json node server.mjs
```

At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts
listening. It exits with code 1 and writes one line to stderr when:

- `PORT` is not made only of ASCII digits `0-9`, or is above `65535`;
- the port cannot be bound (for example, it is already in use);
- the data file cannot be read for any reason other than "does not exist"
  (for example, the path is a directory), or its content is not in the layout
  this server writes (for example, empty or invalid JSON). The line is
  `cannot read data file <name>`, where `<name>` is `DATA_FILE` as given.

A missing data file (or a missing folder on its path) is not an error: the
server starts with no bookings.

### Data handling

- The file is read once, at startup. After that the server's memory is the
  truth; outside edits to the file are not noticed.
- The file is written only when a booking is created or deleted, and each
  change is saved before the reply is sent. The server never creates folders.
- Saves are atomic (write a temporary file next to the data file, then
  rename). If a save fails, the reply is `500 internal error` and nothing
  changes, the next id included. The server keeps running.
- Requests are handled as if one at a time: of several overlapping bookings
  sent at once, exactly one is created and the rest get 409.

## Browser page

Open <http://127.0.0.1:3000/> (adjust the port if you set `PORT`). The page
lets you:

- book a room with a title, date, start and end time (errors from the server
  are shown as-is, for example `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`);
- see the bookings, optionally filtered by date (`Show date`), and clear the
  filter with `Show all`;
- cancel a booking with its `Cancel` button.

The page is `public/index.html` and its script is `public/app.js`, served at
`GET /` and `GET /app.js`.

## API

All JSON replies use `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. Errors
have the body `{"error": "<message>"}`.

A booking looks like this:

```json
{"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
```

Ids start at 1 and increase by one; an id is never reused, even after deletes
and restarts.

Paths are matched byte for byte: no percent-decoding and no slash, dot-segment
or letter-case normalisation. The query string (after the first `?`) is
ignored unless a route says otherwise.

### `GET /api/rooms`

`200`

```json
{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}
```

### `GET /api/bookings`

`200` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room (in the order
above).

```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings
```

```json
{"bookings": [{"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}]}
```

Optional `?date=YYYY-MM-DD` returns only that day's bookings. If `date` is
present but not a valid date (empty included, e.g. `?date` or `?date=`), the
reply is `400 date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. When repeated, the first
`date` is used. Other parameters are ignored.

### `POST /api/bookings`

Body: a JSON object with `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`. Other keys
are ignored. Header `Content-Type: application/json` is required.

```sh
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}'
```

`201` with the new booking:

```json
{"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
```

The rules below are checked in order; the first one that fails decides the
reply.

| #  | Rule                                                                                                   | Status | Error message                                        |
| -- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| 1  | `Content-Type` media type (before the first `;`, trimmed, case-insensitive) is `application/json`     | 415    | `content type must be application/json`              |
| 2  | Body is at most 10000 bytes                                                                            | 413    | `body too large`                                     |
| 3  | Body (UTF-8) parses as a JSON object (not empty, `null`, an array, string, number or boolean; a leading BOM makes it invalid) | 400    | `body must be a JSON object`                         |
| 4  | `room` is exactly one of `Aurora`, `Borealis`, `Cosmos` (case-sensitive)                                | 400    | `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`       |
| 5  | `title` is a string of 1 to 80 UTF-16 code units after trimming; the trimmed title is stored            | 400    | `title must be 1 to 80 characters`                   |
| 6  | `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31 (Feb 29 in years divisible by 4)      | 400    | `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`               |
| 7  | `start` is `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59`                                                            | 400    | `start must be HH:MM`                                |
| 8  | `end` is `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59`                                                              | 400    | `end must be HH:MM`                                  |
| 9  | `end` is later than `start`                                                                            | 400    | `end must be after start`                            |
| 10 | No overlap with a booking of the same room on the same date (back-to-back is fine)                     | 409    | `room is already booked from <start> to <end>`       |

For rule 10, `<start>` and `<end>` are those of the overlapping booking that
starts earliest. Only `title` is trimmed: values such as ` 2026-11-03`,
`2026-11-3` or `9:00` are invalid.

### `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>`

`204` with an empty body; the booking is gone.

```sh
curl -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings/1
```

`404 booking not found` when `<id>` is not a positive integer in ASCII digits
without a leading zero, or no booking has that id.

### Other replies

| Case                                                                                  | Status | Error message          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------- |
| Unknown path, any method (includes `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`)           | 404    | `not found`            |
| Known path with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included), e.g. `GET /api/bookings/abc` | 405    | `method not allowed`   |
| Save failure or any other unexpected error                                            | 500    | `internal error`       |

## Data file

The data file is JSON in this layout:

```json
{
  "nextId": 3,
  "bookings": [
    {"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
  ]
}
```

`nextId` is the id the next booking will get (an integer, at least 1, greater
than every booking id). On startup the file is validated strictly; anything
else makes the server exit with `cannot read data file <name>`.

## Tests

```sh
npm test
```

Runs the `node:test` suites in `test/` (`node --test test/`).

I graded `server.mjs`, `package.json` and `test/server.smoke.test.mjs` against `.team/notes/spec.md` (Server, API, Booking rules) and `.team/notes/decisions.md`. `npm test` passes 60 of 60. The project has no CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or rules files, so only your standards applied. It passes your bar (9 overall, nothing under 7), and I found no spec bugs. The open items are about style and test gaps.

**Spec checks that hold (`/root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/server.mjs`):**
- **Startup order (338–361):** `PORT` is checked first, then the data file is read, then the server listens. Every failure writes one line to stderr and exits with code 1. The port-in-use case is handled with `exitCode` and a natural exit, so there is no stack trace.
- **Data file name and errors:** `DATA_FILE` is echoed exactly as given, and only `ENOENT` means "no bookings yet". A directory, a bad path argument, invalid JSON or the wrong layout all give `cannot read data file <name>`.
- **Body reading (180–191, 303):** the whole body is read and discarded before any routing, so 413 and 415 replies always reach the client. Rule 2 counts the body bytes actually received.
- **Routing (283–312):** paths are compared byte for byte on the raw `req.url` up to the first `?`. `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/` give 404, any other `/api/bookings/<id>` reaches DELETE, and HEAD/OPTIONS give 405. Method lookup uses `Object.hasOwn`, so a method named `constructor` cannot slip through.
- **Booking rules:** they run in order 1 to 10 with the exact messages. Only the title is trimmed. Leap years follow year % 4 inside 2000–2099. The 409 picks the clash that starts earliest, not the first one found (101).
- **Saving (161–172, 235–239):** the temp file sits next to the data file and is then renamed over it, and a failed temp file is cleaned up. Memory, including the next id, only changes after a successful save.
- **Concurrency:** the overlap check and the save run inside one promise queue (229–233), and the queue's error catch does not hide errors from callers.
- **500 handling (314–326):** unexpected errors are logged to stderr only (nothing leaks to the client), the reply is 500 `internal error`, and the server keeps running.
- **Static files and stdout:** static files are served from a fixed map resolved from `import.meta.url`, so there is no path traversal. The listening line is the only stdout write.

# Backend API notes — owner: backend — 2026-11-02

Spec: `.team/notes/spec.md` is the source of truth; this note only records implementation choices.

## Running
- `node server.mjs` (or `npm start`) starts the server. `server.mjs` exports nothing; importing it starts the server.
- Tests: `npm test` runs `node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"`. Plain `node --test test/` does NOT work on Node 22
  (a directory argument is treated as a file). Test files must be named `*.test.mjs` under `test/`;
  helpers in `test/helpers/` are not run as tests.

## Env vars
- `PORT`: unset/empty means 3000. Only ASCII digits, value <= 65535, else one stderr line `invalid PORT: <value>`, exit 1.
  `PORT=0` means the OS picks the port; the stdout line shows the real port.
- `DATA_FILE`: unset/empty means `bookings.json`, resolved against the cwd. ENOENT means start empty (the file is not created).
  Any other read error, or content not in the layout below, gives stderr `cannot read data file <DATA_FILE as given>`, exit 1.
- Bind failure gives stderr `cannot listen on 127.0.0.1:<port>: <code>`, exit 1.
- stdout: only `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>\n`. Unexpected request errors are logged to stderr as one line.

## Data file layout
`{"nextId": <int >= 1>, "bookings": [{"id","room","title","date","start","end"}, ...]}`
Loading is strict: each booking needs exactly those 6 keys, a safe-integer id in 1..nextId-1, unique ids, valid
room/date/times, end > start, an already-trimmed title of 1-80 chars, and no two stored bookings may overlap.
Anything else counts as "not in this server's layout".

## Saving
- Written only on a successful POST create or DELETE remove. Writes `<DATA_FILE>.<pid>.<n>.tmp` in the same folder
  (flag `wx`), then renames it over the data file; on failure the temp file is removed and the reply is 500 `internal error`.
- Memory (bookings and nextId) changes only after the save succeeds. All mutations run one at a time through
  an in-process promise queue (overlap check + save inside the queue).

## Static files
- `GET /` serves `public/index.html` (`text/html; charset=utf-8`), `GET /app.js` serves `public/app.js`
  (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`). Paths are resolved relative to `server.mjs` via `import.meta.url`, read per request.
  A missing file gives 500 `internal error`; the server keeps running. Other methods on these paths get 405.

## Strict readings taken
- ENOTDIR (a path component is a file) is not ENOENT, so it gives `cannot read data file`.
- HEAD on any known path gets 405 (no auto-HEAD for GET routes).
- Overlapping stored bookings in the data file count as an invalid layout.

content.content: # Spec (verbatim from the user) — owner: supervisor Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. Node v22. Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. Page - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. - The page loads the script with a `` is the last element in body. Inline `

# Room bookings

A small meeting-room booking app: one Node.js HTTP server (`server.mjs`) that
serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in a single JSON file.
There are three fixed rooms: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`.

## Requirements

- Node.js 22 or later.
- No dependencies: only Node.js built-ins are used, so there is nothing to
  `npm install`.

## Usage

```sh
npm start
# or
node server.mjs
```

The server listens on `127.0.0.1` only. Once it is listening it prints exactly
one line to stdout, and nothing else ever:

```
listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

The port shown is the one actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS
picked).

### Environment variables

| Variable    | Default         | Meaning                                                                 |
| ----------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. Unset or empty means the default.                    |
| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | Path of the JSON data file. Unset or empty means the default. Relative paths are resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. |

```sh
PORT=8080 DATA_FILE=/var/lib/rooms/bookings.json node server.mjs
```

At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts
listening. It exits with code 1 and writes one line to stderr when:

- `PORT` is not made only of ASCII digits `0-9`, or is above `65535`
  (`invalid PORT: <value>`);
- the port cannot be bound, for example because it is already in use
  (`cannot listen on 127.0.0.1:<port>: <code>`);
- the data file cannot be read for any reason other than "does not exist"
  (for example, the path is a directory), or its content is not in the layout
  this server writes (for example, empty or invalid JSON). The line is
  `cannot read data file <name>`, where `<name>` is `DATA_FILE` as given.

A missing data file (or a missing folder on its path) is not an error: the
server starts with no bookings.

### Data handling

- The file is read once, at startup. After that the server's memory is the
  truth; outside edits to the file are not noticed.
- The file is written only when a booking is created or deleted, and each
  change is saved before the reply is sent. The server never creates folders.
- Saves are atomic (write a temporary file next to the data file, then
  rename). If a save fails, the reply is `500 internal error` and nothing
  changes, the next id included. The server keeps running.
- Requests are handled as if one at a time: of several overlapping bookings
  sent at once, exactly one is created and the rest get 409.

## Browser page

Open <http://127.0.0.1:3000/> (adjust the port if you set `PORT`). The page
lets you:

- book a room with a title, date, start and end time (errors from the server
  are shown as-is, for example `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`);
- see the bookings, optionally filtered by date (`Show date`), and clear the
  filter with `Show all`;
- cancel a booking with its `Cancel` button.

The page is `public/index.html` and its script is `public/app.js`, served at
`GET /` and `GET /app.js`.

## API

All JSON replies use `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. Errors
have the body `{"error": "<message>"}`.

A booking looks like this:

```json
{"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
```

Ids start at 1 and increase by one; an id is never reused, even after deletes
and restarts.

Paths are matched byte for byte: no percent-decoding and no slash, dot-segment
or letter-case normalisation. The query string (after the first `?`) is
ignored unless a route says otherwise.

### `GET /api/rooms`

`200`

```json
{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}
```

### `GET /api/bookings`

`200` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room (in the order
above).

```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings
```

```json
{"bookings": [{"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}]}
```

Optional `?date=YYYY-MM-DD` returns only that day's bookings. If `date` is
present but not a valid date (empty included, e.g. `?date` or `?date=`), the
reply is `400 date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. When repeated, the first
`date` is used. Other parameters are ignored.

### `POST /api/bookings`

Body: a JSON object with `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`. Other keys
are ignored. Header `Content-Type: application/json` is required.

```sh
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}'
```

`201` with the new booking:

```json
{"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
```

The rules below are checked in order; the first one that fails decides the
reply.

| #  | Rule                                                                                                   | Status | Error message                                        |
| -- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| 1  | `Content-Type` media type (before the first `;`, trimmed, case-insensitive) is `application/json`     | 415    | `content type must be application/json`              |
| 2  | Body is at most 10000 bytes                                                                            | 413    | `body too large`                                     |
| 3  | Body (UTF-8) parses as a JSON object (not empty, `null`, an array, string, number or boolean; a leading BOM makes it invalid) | 400    | `body must be a JSON object`                         |
| 4  | `room` is exactly one of `Aurora`, `Borealis`, `Cosmos` (case-sensitive)                                | 400    | `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`       |
| 5  | `title` is a string of 1 to 80 UTF-16 code units after trimming; the trimmed title is stored            | 400    | `title must be 1 to 80 characters`                   |
| 6  | `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31 (Feb 29 in years divisible by 4)      | 400    | `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`               |
| 7  | `start` is `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59`                                                            | 400    | `start must be HH:MM`                                |
| 8  | `end` is `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59`                                                              | 400    | `end must be HH:MM`                                  |
| 9  | `end` is later than `start`                                                                            | 400    | `end must be after start`                            |
| 10 | No overlap with a booking of the same room on the same date (back-to-back is fine)                     | 409    | `room is already booked from <start> to <end>`       |

For rule 10, `<start>` and `<end>` are those of the overlapping booking that
starts earliest. Only `title` is trimmed: values such as ` 2026-11-03`,
`2026-11-3` or `9:00` are invalid.

### `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>`

`204` with an empty body; the booking is gone.

```sh
curl -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings/1
```

`404 booking not found` when `<id>` is not a positive integer in ASCII digits
without a leading zero, or no booking has that id.

### Other replies

| Case                                                                                  | Status | Error message          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------- |
| Unknown path, any method (includes `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`)           | 404    | `not found`            |
| Known path with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included), e.g. `GET /api/bookings/abc` | 405    | `method not allowed`   |
| Save failure or any other unexpected error                                            | 500    | `internal error`       |

## Data file

The data file is JSON in this layout:

```json
{
  "nextId": 3,
  "bookings": [
    {"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
  ]
}
```

`nextId` is the id the next booking will get (an integer, at least 1, greater
than every booking id). On startup the file is validated strictly: every
booking must have exactly the six keys and pass the booking rules (with an
already-trimmed title), ids must be unique, and no two bookings may overlap.
Anything else makes the server exit with `cannot read data file <name>`.

## Tests

```sh
npm test
```

Runs the `node:test` suites in `test/` (`node --test test/`).
